mn71:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Vesāli in the Hall with the peaked roof in the Great Wood.
mn71:2.1: Now on that occasion the Wanderer Vacchagotta was staying in the Wanderers’ Park with the single White-lotus Mango tree.
mn71:3.1: Then when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he went into Vesāli for alms.
mn71:3.3: ‘It is still too early to wander for alms in Vesāli.
mn71:3.4: Suppose I went to the Wanderer Vacchagotta in the Wanderers’ Park with the single White-lotus Mango tree?’
mn71:3.5: Then the Blessed One went to the Wanderer Vacchagotta in the Wanderers’ Park with the single White-lotus Mango tree.
mn71:4.1: The Wanderer Vacchagotta saw the Blessed One coming in the distance.
mn71:4.2: Seeing him, he said to him:
mn71:4.3: “Let the Blessed One come, venerable sir.
mn71:4.4: Welcome to the Blessed One, venerable sir.
mn71:4.5: It is long, venerable sir, since the Blessed One made an occasion to come here.
mn71:4.6: Let the Blessed One be seated, venerable sir; this seat is ready.”
mn71:4.7: The Blessed One sat down on the seat made ready.
mn71:4.8: And Vacchagotta the Wanderer took another, lower, seat and sat down at one side.
mn71:4.9: When he had done so, Vacchagotta the Wanderer said to the Blessed One:
mn71:5.2: ‘the recluse Gotama is omniscient and all-seeing, he claims to have complete knowledge and vision thus:
mn71:5.3: “whether I am walking or standing or asleep or awake, my knowledge and vision are continuously and unceasingly maintained.”’
mn71:5.4: Venerable sir, when they who say that say: ‘the recluse Gotama is omniscient and all-seeing, he claims to have complete knowledge and vision thus: “whether I am walking or standing or asleep or awake, my knowledge and vision are continuously and unceasingly maintained” ’ — do they, venerable sir, say what the Blessed One says, without misrepresenting the Blessed One with what is not so, do they express a dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and does no legitimate deduction from their assertion give ground for censure?”
mn71:5.5: “Vaccha, those who say thus: ‘the recluse Gotama is omniscient and all-seeing, he claims to have complete knowledge and vision thus: “whether I am walking or standing or asleep or awake, my knowledge and vision are continuously and unceasingly maintained” ’ — they do not say what I say, and they misrepresent me with what is not true and not so.”
mn71:6.1: “Venerable sir, how then should we answer so as to say what the Blessed One says, without misrepresenting the Blessed One with what is not so, and express a dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no legitimate deduction from our assertion would give ground for censure?”
mn71:6.2: “Vaccha, if you answer thus: ‘the recluse Gotama has the three true knowledges’[^1] — you would be saying what I say, without misrepresenting me with what is not so, you would express a dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and no legitimate deduction from your assertion would give ground for censure.
mn71:7.1: For, Vaccha, as far as I want, I recollect my manifold past lives,
mn71:7.2: that is, one birth, two births … thus with their aspects and particulars I recollect my manifold past lives.
mn71:8.1: And, Vaccha, as far as I want, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, I see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate … I understand how beings pass on according to their actions.
mn71:9.1: And, Vaccha, by realizing for myself with direct knowledge, I here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.
mn71:10.1: If you answer thus: ‘the recluse Gotama has the three true knowledges’ — you would be saying what I say, without misrepresenting me with what is not so, you would express a dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and no legitimate deduction from your assertion would give ground for censure.”
mn71:11.1: When this was said, the Wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One:
mn71:11.2: “Master Gotama, is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, makes an end of suffering on the dissolution of the body?”
mn71:11.3: “There is no householder, Vaccha, who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, makes an end of suffering on the dissolution of the body.”
mn71:12.1: “But, Master Gotama, is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, on the dissolution of the body passes on to heaven?”
mn71:12.2: “Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred, but far more are the householders who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, on the dissolution of the body pass on to heaven.”
mn71:13.1: “Master Gotama, is there any Ājīvaka ascetic[^2] who on the dissolution of the body makes an end of suffering?”
mn71:13.2: “There is no Ājīvaka ascetic, Vaccha, who on the dissolution of the body makes an end of suffering.”
mn71:14.1: “But, Master Gotama, is there any Ājīvaka ascetic who on the dissolution of the body passes on to heaven?”
mn71:14.2: “Ninety-one aeons back, Vaccha, as far as I recollect, I know of no Ājīvaka ascetic who passed on to heaven on the dissolution of the body, except for one,
mn71:14.3: and he too was a teacher of the doctrine of action and the doctrine of doing.”
mn71:15.1: “That being so, Master Gotama, this other sectarians’ basis is empty,
mn71:15.2: even of a chance of passing on to heaven!”
mn71:15.3: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn71:15.4: The Wanderer Vacchagotta was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
